newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended slightly higher across the board on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Friday.

"Treasury bill yields ended mixed today but bond prices ended slightly higher across the board. The interbank rate went up but it did not attract a lot of players. Volume was only moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at an unchanged yield from Thursday of 1.90/1.85 percent and one-year closed at a yield of 2.07/2.02 percent against 2.12/2.07 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.48/98.53 from Thursday's close of S$98.35/98.40, September 2001 at S$97.15/97.20 versus S$97.05/97.10 and June 2003 at S$95.15/95.20 against S$95.05/95.10.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/8 3-0/0 percent from Thursday's 3-0/0 2-7/8 percent.
